Consider the graph of the function $f(x),$ shown above. It consists of three line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $3$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [0,0.5]$, the piecewise linear for $x\in [0.5,2],$ and the piecewise linear for $x\in [2,4].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{0}^{0.5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0.5}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,0.5].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 0.5\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0.5,2].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{0.5}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-\frac{3}{2}.
$$

The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [2,4].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{3}{2}+2 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{3}{2}+2\cdot \frac{2}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{4}{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
